about: A workflow every account can find and run: take anything a person shares (a post, a thread, an article, a video, a repository, a product page) and put each part where it can be used. Methods become technique records, step-by-step playbooks become workflow recipes, code becomes tools, and paid products become free or open-source tools that do the same job. One workflow-recipe row in the shape of the shared recipe shelf (job, input_schema, ordered steps, each with do, submit and checks).

payload.produces: New technique records, recipes and tools made from what was shared, with the free tool for each paid one; "what I took from this and built" is a post.
payload.label: Turn something shared into what you can use
payload.job: Read what the person shared in full, split it into its parts, and put each part where the person's AI can use it again: methods and facts as technique records described by what they work on (never tied to one medium), step-by-step playbooks as workflow recipes, code as tools, and every paid product matched to a free or open-source tool that does the same job. Record every step that is not adopted and why.

source.name: Anything shared means incorporate it, not acknowledge it
source.note: Written from the way one person's AI handled 30 shared posts, repositories and product pages on 2026-10-30: each was split into parts and each part went to the owner of its kind. Steps that deceive people or evade a platform's checks are recorded as not adopted with the reason, never silently dropped.

shared.description: What the person shared: each item is a link, or the pasted text of a post or article. Left out when the run was woken by a shared record: the gather step reads it from the record.

why.description: Anything the person said about it, in their own words (for example 'must do 100%')

steps.title: Gather what was shared
steps.do: If the input names shared, use it as it is, and the input why as why. Otherwise the run was woken by the person sharing something: for each change in the run's cause (task.cause.detail.changes) whose id starts with shared: and is not deleted, call records:read with { "id": <that id> }. From each record's value.items take every link's url, every selection's text, and every file's file identity; that list is shared. The record's value.own_words, when it has them, is why (join the words of several records with a blank line).

steps.title: Read every item in full
steps.do: For each item in shared from the gather step: if it is pasted text, use it as it is. If it is a link, call tool:read-public-web-page with { "url": <the link> }. If that tool reports the page needs a signed-in browser (for example x.com or reddit.com), call tool:read-a-page-in-my-browser with the same url. Read the whole thing, including replies or linked articles that the item points to as its main content. For a video, get its words: use the platform's captions if the page has them; otherwise use the transcription tool the person has (a tools-from-github row such as whisper) on the downloaded audio. Record for each item: the url (or 'pasted'), its author, and its full text.

steps.title: Split it into parts and name each part's kind
steps.do: Go through the text of every item and list its parts. Each part is exactly one of: 'method' (a way of doing something that works on some property, such as hooks, timing, layout, pricing or verification), 'playbook' (an ordered procedure someone can follow step by step), 'code' (a repository, package or script), 'paid-product' (a product or service that charges), 'claim' (a number or result the author reports), or 'reference' (a list of examples, styles or components). Write each part in your own words; do not copy the author's prose. For every claim, keep the number and mark it as the author's claim, not a fact.

checks.says: Every part comes from something that was read

steps.title: Make every part generic, ask what a 1000x version would be, and find everything else it applies to
steps.do: For every part from the split step, answer these questions and write the answers down. (1) Make it generic: rewrite the part so that no medium (video, slides, a web page), product, platform or person is part of it. Test: delete every name and every medium word; if the part no longer says what to do, it is still tied to one case, so rewrite it again. (2) Say why it works: 'mechanism' is what it does to a person or to a system, in words that fit any medium (for example 'an open promise the person wants kept holds their attention until it is kept'). 'operates_on' is the abstract property it changes (for example attention, trust, timing, effort, cost, error rate). 'needs' lists what must already be true for it to work. 'produces' is the effect it has when it works. (3) Reuse terms: before you write a mechanism or an operates_on term, search the person's technique records for the closest existing term with the person's search tool. Use the existing term when it means the same thing. Add a new term only when no existing term fits, and record each new term with the reason in new_terms. (4) Ask what a 1000x version would be: not a bigger copy, but the version that removes the need for the part, makes it happen by itself, or makes it work for every case at once. Then judge the part by what it actually makes possible, not by how complete it looks, and apply the same question to the way you are doing this step. (5) Find everything else it applies to: list at least three other media or jobs where the same mechanism works (for example a sales demo, an onboarding screen, a document, a lesson, a support reply), each with one sentence on how. A part that applies to only one medium has not been made generic yet; go back to (1).

checks.says: Every part from the split step was made generic
Every generic part is one of the parts that were split out

steps.title: Check what the person already has before adding anything
steps.do: For each part, search the person's existing technique records, workflow recipes and tools for one that does the same job: use the person's search tool on their records with the part's generic text and its mechanism (from the make-generic step) as the question, and list the Workshop tools. If one exists, mark the part 'already-have' with its id and say whether the new part improves it. Never add a second record, recipe or tool for a job that already has one; improve the existing one instead.

steps.title: Find the free or open-source tool for every paid product
steps.do: For each paid-product part: write its job in one plain sentence. Search for open-source repositories and free tools that do that job (GitHub search for the job's words, and the person's existing Workshop tools). For each candidate record the repository, its licence as read from the repository's own licence file (never guessed), whether it runs on the person's own computer, and how close it comes to the paid product. If no free tool does the job, describe what the paid product shows on its public pages and public app files and what a tool would need to do the same; never sign up, pay, or install the paid product to find out.

steps.title: Name every step you will not adopt, and why
steps.do: Go through every playbook and method part. Any step that deceives people (pretending, hiding who you are or that you are selling), evades a platform's spam or safety checks, breaks a site's rules or a law, or copies someone's words or designs instead of their structure, is not adopted. For each, record the step, the reason, and the honest version if there is one. Everything else is adopted.

steps.title: Write every process as a recipe that runs, with what wakes it
steps.do: For each playbook part from the split step that the check-what-exists step marked new or improves-existing, and for each method part that is something a person does again and again (a weekly review, a follow-up, a refresh, a launch), write one workflow recipe in the shape of the shared recipe shelf (the Workshop's tools/workflows README, 'Recipe shape'): id (workflow: and lowercase words with dashes), label, job, source (the shared item it came from, and the steps not adopted with their reasons from the not-adopted step), input_schema with every detail that changes from person to person (names, products, places, amounts, platforms, thresholds), and ordered steps. Each step's do names the exact Workshop tool id it calls (list the Workshop tools; a step no tool does is done by the AI and says so), the exact input it gives, and which of the person's records it reads (by record kind); each step has a submit schema for what it hands back and checks from the Workshop's recipe-check-kinds.json that bind its output to earlier steps or the input. Then give the recipe its wake, read from the playbook's own words about when it happens: a rhythm ('every Monday', 'each quarter') is a time cause with every_ms and from_ms; a thing the person writes down or saves (a launch date, a new recording, a request) is a record cause on resource own-records with the record's kind; something that comes in from outside is an arrival cause with its source; something the computer notices (a card or drive connected, an app opened) is a host_event cause of a kind the Workshop's recipe-wake-causes.json lists. Each wake has an id, a budget of steps and wall_ms (at least that file's least_budget, at most the ledger its cause draws from), and input.start_at naming the step a woken run starts at. A process with no rhythm or event of its own gets no wake; say why in no_wake_because. Write produces: one line saying what a run makes that could be shared. Check every recipe with the recipe validator (recipeProblems in the Workshop's tools/workflows/read-data/recipe-problems.mjs) until it reports no problems; never name a person, product, number or place of the person's own inside a recipe meant for everyone.

checks.says: Every recipe is written from a part that was split out

steps.title: Put each part where it can be used again
steps.do: For each part marked new or improves-existing: a method, claim or reference becomes a technique record in the person's techniques list with id, name, kind, a description in your own words, source_url, author, and the fields from the make-generic step: mechanism, operates_on, needs, produces and applies_to, using the existing terms that step chose (never a field limited to one medium such as video). A playbook is the recipe the write-recipes step wrote: save it with the person's record write as a workflow-recipe record, and offer the ones meant for everyone to the shared recipe shelf. Code that does a job with an input and an output becomes a Workshop tool or a tools-from-github row with its licence read from the repository. A free option from the free-instead-of-paid step becomes a tools-from-github row the same way. Use the person's record write for records; show the person each recipe and tool before it is shared publicly.

steps.title: Tell the person what went where
steps.do: Call tool:tell-the-person with a short message: for each shared item, what was built from it and where (technique records with their count, recipes, tools), the free tools found for each paid product, the steps not adopted with their reasons, and anything that needs the person (an account, a payment, approving a public recipe). Give exact names and places, never just 'saved'.
